sentences.text: Coram:

Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnish Bhatnagar
 Order

The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. by the petitioners for quashing of FIR No.222/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Burari and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 20.11.2020 according to Hindu rites and customs and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since April 2021.
On 22.02.2022, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/09/2023 at 21:15:23 4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, with the intervention of elderly persons, the respondent no. 2 and petitioner no. 1 have settled the matter amicably and they are living together from the last seven months.

In this regard settlement dated Rahul Rawat And Others vs The State And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172439322/
1 25.02.2023 is already on record.

sentences.text: 5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by their counsels.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent no.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioner no. 1 and she is living happily with her husband.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
Respondent no.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement and as the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are living happily together separately in a rented accommodation, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.
Consequentially, this petition is allowed and of FIR No.222/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Burari, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/09/2023 at 21:15:23 8.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J SEPTEMBER 18, 2023/ib
